text:
jordan: CI started failing after we bumped to redwood-sdk[streaming]==0.9.1. Local dev env works, but Docker builds error with ImportError: No module named 'redwood.streams'.

jordan: repro steps in CI Dockerfile:
```Dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
COPY pyproject.toml poetry.lock /app/
RUN pip install --upgrade pip 
RUN pip install 'redwood-sdk[streaming]==0.9.1'
```

jordan: CI pip log shows this (truncated):
```
Processing ./wheels/redwood_sdk-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl
Installing collected packages: redwood-sdk
Successfully installed redwood-sdk-0.9.1
```

jordan: note there is no httpx or any streaming deps installed in the log. Local venv when I run `pip install 'redwood-sdk[streaming]==0.9.1'` pulls httpx, sseclient, etc.

dev-support: thanks — is your CI pulling wheels from an internal cache/registry or building wheels locally? also what pip version in CI?

jordan: CI uses our internal artifact proxy (nexus) that caches wheels published by the build pipeline. pip 23.3 in the image. I can run `pip install -vvv` in CI if that helps.

marta: can you run two quick checks inside the failed CI container?
1) `python -c "import pkg_resources; print(pkg_resources.get_distribution('redwood-sdk').extras)"`
2) `unzip -p /path/to/wheel/redwood_sdk-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl METADATA | grep Provides-Extra || true`

jordan: ran those in a debug job, outputs below:
```
>>> import pkg_resources
>>> pkg_resources.get_distribution('redwood-sdk').extras
[]
$ unzip -p wheels/redwood_sdk-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl METADATA | grep Provides-Extra || true
# (no output)
```

jordan: so the wheel in our cache doesn't have any `Provides-Extra` metadata. Local pip wheel from PyPI does.

alex: that explains it — pip only installs extras listed in wheel METADATA. If the cached wheel was built without extras metadata (our internal build step), extras won't be pulled by `pip install 'package[extra]'` because pip thinks the wheel has no extras.

marta: thanks for the verification. short-term workaround: explicitly install streaming deps before/alongside SDK in the Dockerfile: `pip install httpx==0.24.0 sseclient-py` or `pip install 'redwood-sdk==0.9.1' && pip install httpx...`

marta: long-term: I'm opening a ticket with infra to fix the wheel publishing step so METADATA contains `Provides-Extra: streaming` entries. we should also add a CI gate to verify METADATA for published wheels. :white_check_mark:

dev-support: can you attach the internal wheel (redwood_sdk-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl) so infra can inspect the builder logs? ci-bot: uploaded artifact at https://nexus.internal/wheels/redwood_sdk-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl

jordan: applied the workaround in the Dockerfile and CI green for now. thanks.

marta: follow-up: action items -> (1) infra ticket to fix wheel builder, (2) add METADATA check to release job, (3) publish fixed wheel and bump cached artifact. I'll post ticket link in this thread.

alex: note for teams: if you see inconsistent import behavior between local/dev vs cached wheels in CI, check wheel METADATA and don't assume extras were preserved during internal republishing.

jordan: huge help, appreciate it! :pray:
